story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Import all modules into CLI command (fetch, consolidate, analyze, edge, stake, render) 2. Execute pipeline in order: fetch → consolidate → analyze → edge → stake → render 3. Pass data between layers without errors or data loss 4. Accept bankroll from CLI argument (--bankroll, required, positive float) 5. Log execution time for each phase (fetch, consolidate, analyze, edge, stake, render) 6. Handle exceptions at top level without crashing CLI 7. Return proper exit codes (0 success, 1 error) 8. Integrate error handler display from Story 7.3 for user-friendly error messages 9. Integrate formatter and renderer from Stories 7.1-7.2 for output display 10. Support optional --threshold flag for EV threshold override (default 5%) 11. Support optional --league flag to filter fixtures by league 12. Verify all data flows correctly through each layer with logging

doc.title: Technical Specification
doc.section: High-Level Flow, System Architecture, Module Breakdown, Error Handling Strategy
doc.snippet: Pipeline sequence: User input → Data fetch → Consolidation → OpenAI → Edge detection → Display. Error handling: Graceful degradation (continue with partial data when possible). Performance: Total runtime target < 2 minutes for 20-30 fixtures. Logging: Track each phase's execution time and data quality.

doc.title: Requirements Document
doc.section: User Stories & Acceptance Criteria, Success Metrics, Constraints & Requirements
doc.snippet: Tool identifies current date/time at runtime. Pulls all fixtures for today. Consolidates fixture data. Handles API failures gracefully. Analysis scope: Same-day matches ONLY. Execution model: Batch processing, on-demand. Analysis speed: Complete in < 2 minutes for typical fixture volume. Edge threshold: 5% minimum EV for recommendation.

doc.title: Story 7.1: Terminal Formatter
doc.section: Implementation Summary, Main Function, Display Output
doc.snippet: Formatter returns Rich-formatted table string with columns: Fixture, Market, AI Prob, Implied Prob, EV, Confidence, Stake. Function signature: format_picks_for_display(picks: list[Pick]) → str. Handles empty picks with user-friendly message. Includes summary footer with statistics (picks count, avg EV, avg confidence, total stake, EV range).

doc.title: Story 7.2: Results Renderer
doc.section: Implementation Summary, State Handlers, Output States
doc.snippet: Renders final analysis results with 5 states: PICKS_FOUND (green success), NO_PICKS_AVAILABLE (neutral), NO_MATCHES_TODAY (info), ERROR (red failure), DEGRADED (yellow warning). Function signature: async render_analysis_results(picks: list[Pick] | None, bankroll: float, data_quality: dict) → str. Integrates formatter output, adds data quality notes and next steps guidance.

doc.title: Story 7.3: Error Display Handler
doc.section: Implementation Summary, Error Categories, User-Friendly Messages
doc.snippet: Categorizes errors into 5 types: API (401/403/404/429/5xx), Network (timeout/connection), Validation (Pydantic), Configuration (missing keys), System (permissions/disk). Function signature: display_error(error: Exception, context: dict | None) → str. Returns user-friendly messages with actionable guidance. Logs full error details while showing simplified user message.

file.reason: Main CLI command that orchestrates entire pipeline. This story implements the core logic here.
Phase 1: Data fetching. Story imports and calls this to get raw fixtures from all sources (API-Football, ESPN, FlashScore, Odds-API).
Phase 2: Data consolidation. Normalizes, validates freshness, merges data from multiple sources. Story calls this after Phase 1.
Phase 3: AI Analysis. Calls OpenAI for each fixture to estimate probabilities. Story calls this after Phase 2.
Phase 4: Edge Detection. Calculates EV, applies confidence scoring, filters by threshold. Story calls this after Phase 3.
Phase 5: Stake Sizing. Recommends stake sizes based on bankroll, EV, and confidence. Story calls this after Phase 4.
Phase 6a: Display formatting. Converts Pick list to Rich-formatted table. Story imports and uses this for output formatting.
Phase 6b: Results rendering. Wraps formatter output with state-aware header, summary, data quality notes, next steps. Story imports and uses this for final output.
Error display. Formats exceptions into user-friendly messages. Story catches exceptions and calls this to display helpful error info.
Exception classes used throughout pipeline. Story catches and handles these in top-level error handler.
Logging infrastructure. Story uses this for phase timing and debug logging. Imported from Story 1.5.
Data structures passed between layers. Story works with these models through entire pipeline.
API keys and configuration. Story uses Config to get OPENAI_API_KEY and API_FOOTBALL_KEY.

constraint.description: Pipeline execution order is MANDATORY: fetch → consolidate → analyze → edge → stake → render. Data flows sequentially through layers without circular dependencies.
constraint.source: Story 8.1 AC#2, Technical Spec High-Level Flow

constraint.description: Critical errors (auth failure, no fixtures) halt pipeline. Degradation errors (stale data, missing injuries) continue with flag. Individual errors (single fixture fails) skip item but continue. Top-level catch prevents CLI crash.
constraint.source: Technical Spec Error Handling Strategy, Story 8.1 AC#6

constraint.description: Return exit code 0 for success (any output state: picks found, no picks, no matches). Return exit code 1 for critical error (API auth failed, exception unhandled). Graceful degradation states (partial data loss) return 0.
Total pipeline execution time must be < 2 minutes for typical fixture volume (20-30 fixtures). Each phase should be timing-measured for optimization. Async I/O prevents blocking on network calls.
constraint.source: Requirements AC#1, Technical Spec Performance & Scaling

constraint.description: --bankroll is REQUIRED (float, positive, min=$1). --threshold is OPTIONAL (float, default 5.0%, range 0-100%). --league is OPTIONAL (string, optional league filter). All inputs validated before pipeline execution.

Use formatter (Story 7.1) for pick table. Use renderer (Story 7.2) for final output with state awareness. Use error_handler (Story 7.3) for exception display. All output goes to terminal via Rich console.

Consolidation layer validates: odds must be <1h old, injuries <12h old, form <24h old. Stale data flags confidence reduction, not pipeline halt. Validation errors (required field missing) halt with error.
constraint.source: Requirements Data Freshness Requirements, Technical Spec Data Quality Rules

constraint.description: EV threshold (default 5%) is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Edge detection must filter picks with EV < threshold. CLI --threshold override must be ≥0% and ≤100%. Threshold failure returns NO_PICKS state, not error.
All layer modules must be importable without circular dependencies. CLI only imports public APIs from each layer. No private _impl modules exposed.
constraint.source: Story 8.1 AC#1, Technical Spec Module Breakdown

interface.name: fetch_all_data()
interface.description: Returns dict with keys: 'fixtures' (list of raw fixture objects), optional error tracking for degraded sources. Called as Phase 1 in pipeline.

interface.name: consolidate_fixtures()
interface.signature: async def consolidate_fixtures(raw_data: dict) → tuple[list[Fixture], dict]
interface.description: Returns tuple: (consolidated Fixture list, data_quality dict tracking success/failure of each source). Called as Phase 2 in pipeline.

interface.name: analyze_all_fixtures()
interface.description: Returns list of Fixture objects with AIAnalysis added to each. Handles individual fixture failures gracefully (marks as failed, continues). Called as Phase 3 in pipeline.

interface.name: detect_edges()
interface.signature: def detect_edges(fixtures: list[Fixture], threshold: float = 5.0, league_filter: str | None = None) → list[Pick]
interface.description: Returns list of Pick objects meeting EV threshold. Applies confidence scoring. Supports optional league filtering. Called as Phase 4 in pipeline.

interface.name: calculate_stakes()
interface.signature: def calculate_stakes(picks: list[Pick], bankroll: float) → list[Pick]
interface.description: Returns list of Pick objects with recommended_stake populated. Uses formula: bankroll × (EV_pct * 0.1) × (confidence/100). Called as Phase 5 in pipeline.

interface.name: format_picks_for_display()
interface.description: Returns Rich-formatted table string with columns: Fixture, Market, AI Prob, Implied Prob, EV, Confidence, Stake. Handles empty picks with helpful message. Called as Phase 6a in pipeline.

interface.name: render_analysis_results()
interface.signature: async def render_analysis_results(picks: list[Pick] | None, bankroll: float, data_quality: dict) → str
interface.description: Returns final formatted output string with state-aware header, formatted picks (via formatter), summary stats, data quality notes, next steps. Called as Phase 6b in pipeline.

interface.name: display_error()
interface.signature: def display_error(error: Exception, context: dict | None = None) → str
interface.description: Returns formatted error message string. Categorizes error (API, Network, Validation, Config, System) and provides user-friendly guidance with actionable next steps. Used in exception handlers.

interface.name: analyze (CLI command)
interface.signature: @app.command() async def analyze(bankroll: float, threshold: float = 5.0, league: str | None = None, verbose: bool = False) → int
interface.description: Main CLI entry point. Orchestrates entire pipeline. Returns exit code (0 success, 1 error). Implemented in this story.

tests.standards: Testing standards for bet-bot follow pytest with Pydantic model fixtures and asyncio.run() for async functions. Unit tests use mocking (unittest.mock) to isolate functions. Integration tests use real data structures and verify end-to-end pipeline. Tests validate: correct output types, proper error handling, logging output, performance within targets (<2 min), exit codes. Minimum 80% code coverage required. Use Rich console capture for display output testing.
tests.locations: /tests/unit/ - Unit test files using pytest and mocks /tests/integration/ - Integration test files using real data /tests/fixtures/ - Reusable test data (sample fixtures, responses, etc) Focus areas: CLI argument parsing, all 6 phases, error handling, timing, exit codes
tests.ideas: AC#1 (Import modules): Test all imports work without circular dependencies AC#2 (Pipeline order): Test phase execution sequence, data flows between phases AC#3 (No data loss): Test each phase receives correct data from previous phase AC#4 (Bankroll arg): Test valid/invalid inputs, validation errors AC#5 (Phase timing): Test execution time measurements, logging, performance target <2 min AC#6 (Exception handling): Test top-level catch prevents crash, proper error handling at each phase AC#7 (Exit codes): Test return 0 on success, 1 on critical error, graceful degradation returns 0 AC#8 (Error display): Test display_error() called for exceptions, user-friendly messages shown AC#9 (Formatter/Renderer): Test output displays correctly, picks formatted as table, states (picks found/no picks/error) work AC#10 (Threshold override): Test --threshold arg accepted, overrides default 5%, validated 0-100% AC#11 (League filter): Test --league arg accepted, passed to edge detection, filters fixtures AC#12 (Data flow logging): Test logging shows fixtures → consolidated → analyzed → picks at each phase
